name: Natosuelta

attributes.attribute: Continental Celtic goddess of fresh water
name means meandering river or winding brook
ruled by the watershed of Natosuelta
guardian of the home and hearth

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Natosuelta, also written Nantosuelta, was a Continental Celtic goddess of fresh water. Her name has been read as meandering river or winding brook. Like other river goddesses she held sway over the ground fed by her stream, here the River Trent in Britain. Roman-era images do not press her river nature. They show her holding a pot, a sign that she guarded the hearth and the domestic realm. Some images place a house on a pole, with a raven, the symbol of prophecy, perched on it. A shrine to her rose at the Roman town of Ad Pontem, which is East Stoke in Nottinghamshire. There she appeared beside an unnamed male god. On the European mainland she was at times joined with the god Sucellus.

okr.objective: Natosuelta is a Continental Celtic goddess of fresh water and the home.
